build: Two Mastertronic G64 disk variants, with disk IDs AD and TO

comments.text: Checks disk selector 6 before exchanging the staging space. Other selectors take the exchange path directly.
Selects VIC bank $8000 and the screen matrix at $8800. Turns the display on before it prints nine characters.
Copies GAME OVER from $1564 to the screen at $89EF and writes white to each cell's colour RAM. An original AD run stopped here and drew the same pixels as TO's separate routine at $811D.
Delays with two eight-bit counters after drawing the message. Once the outer counter reaches $FF, branches to the load path via $156D.
Nine screen codes spelling GAME OVER, copied by $1540 into the display.
Turns off the display, then rejoins the normal file transition at $1527.

Stores the requested resource index at $19B7. Resets video, sound, and colour state for loading, chooses KERNAL banking and then jumps to the transition code at $1520. This entry uses an A-to-memory save where the TO loader places the selector on the stack.
Stores the selector saved at the start of the AD loading path; $19EC doubles the value to read the filename and destination pairs.
Selects RAM under the chips and exchanges $55 pages starting at $2C00 and $8600. Restores the KERNAL and I/O mapping after the exchange.
Doubles the selector from $19B7, loads the destination operand pair from $1A31 and filename from $1A45, configures logical file and drive 8, then calls KERNAL LOAD and jumps to the exchange routine.
Operand of the LDX at $1A1E. The loader writes the selected file destination's low byte here before calling KERNAL LOAD.
Operand of the LDY at $1A20. The loader writes the selected file destination's high byte here before calling KERNAL LOAD.
Reads VIC control 1, sets the display enable bit and returns. This helper follows the unconditional jump back to the staging swap.
Ten little-endian starting addresses copied into the LDX and LDY immediate operands of KERNAL LOAD.
The loader reads the high byte of the same words whose low bytes start at $1A31, using the selector times two as the index.
Ten two-byte names. The two bytes at $1A59 hold the active name passed to SETNAM.
Second characters in the inline file names. The loader reads them every two bytes.
First of the two filename bytes passed to KERNAL SETNAM, filled when a selector is handled.
Second filename byte in the same buffer. The loader copies it from the second-character table at $1A46.
